chapters.title: 01 · Architecture
chapters.text: ESP32 runs the loop. The iPhone app and web console handle setup, tasks, and monitoring.

chapters.title: 02 · Sign in
chapters.text: DEMO-TOKEN is a sample credential. No real device credentials appear in this video.

chapters.title: 03 · Monitor and trace
chapters.text: Phone view on the left, execution trace on the right. Clarity first, with a 5-second refresh interval.

chapters.title: 04 · Start with an example
chapters.text: Choose from 12 read-only goals, plus a screen-reading task that needs no HID control.

chapters.title: 05 · Let the goal guide each step
chapters.text: Each round combines a fresh frame, recent actions, and the expected result to choose one action.

chapters.title: 05 · Let the goal guide each step
chapters.text: Each round combines a fresh frame, recent actions, and the expected result to choose one action.

chapters.title: 06 · Verify completion
chapters.text: An HID acknowledgment alone is insufficient. A new frame must confirm the full goal.

chapters.title: 07 · Start a separate recovery example
chapters.text: A new simulated task demonstrates recovery from a stall. The completed task stays finished.

chapters.title: 07 · Replan or stop
chapters.text: Retry and action limits prevent endless loops. Stop takes priority over late model responses.

chapters.title: 08 · Shared model settings
chapters.text: Endpoint, model, and key are stored on ESP32. This demo uses an example domain and sends no cloud requests.

chapters.title: 09 · Reproducible and transparent
chapters.text: Fixtures ship with the source. Physical HID operation still needs a host adapter, mirroring, and pointer calibration.
